sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: World Monitor is a real-time global intelligence dashboard. It gathers news, geopolitical events, markets, military flights, cyber and climate data into maps and panels, with AI-written briefs.
sixtySeconds.problem: Following world events means jumping between dozens of news sites, maps and market tools. World Monitor brings those streams together and highlights where signals converge, in a web app, desktop app or terminal.
whoFor: Analysts and researchers tracking global events
Investors watching markets, commodities and risk
Self-hosters who want their own situational dashboard
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a free, open-source situation dashboard you can use online, in the terminal or self-host. It supports local AI through Ollama so no API keys are required.
requirements: Optional: credentials for some data sources (see .env.example)

overview: World Monitor aggregates curated global and regional news feeds and summarises them into AI briefs. It shows events on a 3D globe or flat WebGL map, correlates military, economic, disaster and escalation signals, and tracks a Country Instability Index for 31 countries.

A finance radar covers stock exchanges, commodities and crypto. Site variants for tech, finance, commodities, energy and positive news are built from the same codebase. The UI is multilingual with right-to-left support, and AI features can run locally with Ollama.

You can use the public website, a Tauri desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux, a terminal dashboard with npx worldmonitor, a CLI, SDKs for Python, Ruby and Go, or an MCP server. The README asks that forks not present themselves as the official site.

troubleshooting.problem: npm install fails with Invalid comparator
troubleshooting.solution: You're on an old Node.js (for example Debian 12's Node 18). Install Node.js 24 as pinned in .nvmrc.
